key_insight: STEP3-VL-10B demonstrates that a compact (≈10B) open-source foundation model can reach frontier-level multimodal capability by jointly training a language-aligned Perception Encoder with a Qwen3-8B decoder on massive multimodal data and then applying a scaled post-training pipeline.
problem_solved: Bridges the trade-off between model compactness and multimodal intelligence — enabling strong vision-language performance without requiring very large, frozen backbones or prohibitive compute for downstream alignment.
method: Unified, fully unfrozen pre-training on ~1.2T multimodal tokens that integrates a language-aligned Perception Encoder with a Qwen3-8B decoder to build intrinsic vision–language synergy.
Scaled post-training pipeline with extensive iterative fine-tuning (over 1k post-training iterations) for alignment and instruction-following.
Lightweight 10B architecture and open-source release to prioritize deployment efficiency and community-driven development.
impact: Provides practitioners an efficient, deployable multimodal foundation model that lowers compute and development barriers for vision-language research and applications, accelerating experimentation and production use.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: Perception Encoder → Qwen3-8B decoder pipeline highlighting the unified, unfrozen training flow.
Training timeline: pre-training (1.2T multimodal tokens) followed by scaled post-training (over 1k iterative steps).
Trade-off chart: model size vs multimodal capability showing STEP3-VL-10B positioned for high capability at compact size.
Icons/metrics panel: open-source badge, compute/latency indicators, and sample multimodal task examples (captioning, VQA, instruction following).
paper_authors: Ailin Huang, Chengyuan Yao, Chunrui Han, Fanqi Wan, Hangyu Guo
